sentences.text: Shri Madan Singh - Advocate for the petitioner.

Ms. Shanti Tiwari - Panel Lawyer for the State.
 Order

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.78/2024 dated 18.03.2024 registered at Police Station -Amlai, District Shahdol for the offence under Sections 363, 366-A, 344,
376, 376 (3), 376 (2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5-L/6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and under Sections 3 (1)(W)(ii) and 3 (2) (v) of SC and ST Act.
2 .

Learned counsel for the applicant contends that as per the prosecution story, the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C makes it abundantly clear that prosecutrix and applicant were known to each other for more than a year and were constantly in touch through social media.

The prosecutrix also intended to enter into wedlock with the applicant, however,
subsequently the applicant has been implicated.
It is contended by the counsel that the applicant is aged about 22 having no criminal past.
Therefore, the applicant who is in custody since 7.7.2024 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40416 2 MCRC-34090-2024 deserves to be enlarged on bail.
3. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail and submitted that considering the nature of allegation, no case for grant of bail is made out.

sentences.text: 4. Considering the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and perusal of the record reflects that the prosecutrix in her statement stated that she was known to the applicant for more than 1 year and was in touch constantly through social media and accordingly developed relationship.
The applicant is in custody since 7.7.2024 having no criminal past.
Thus, considering the totality of the circumstances, the application is allowed.

5. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned their appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.
6. It is further directed that the applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 480 (3) of the BNSS, 2023.
7. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
